binders: There exists a real constant C.
Universally quantified thereafter are a type Ω equipped with a measurable space, a measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance, a sequence X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ, and a natural number N.
hypotheses: Every coordinate function X_i is measurable.

Let qμ(Y) be the ENNReal infimum of all t such that Y is measurable, 0 < t < ∞ in the endpoint-exclusion sense t ≠ 0 and t ≠ ∞, exp(Y²/t.toReal²) is μ-integrable, and its integral is at most 2. Let K = sup_{i∈ℕ} qμ(X_i). The hypothesis is K < ∞.
conclusions: The function M_N(ω) = max_{0≤i<N} |X_i(ω)| is μ-integrable.
Its integral satisfies ∫ M_N dμ ≤ C · K.toReal · sqrt(log(N)), where N is cast to a real before applying log.
mathematical_definitions: qμ(Y) = inf {t ∈ ENNReal | Y is measurable, t ≠ 0, t ≠ ∞, exp(Y²/t.toReal²) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(Y²/t.toReal²) dμ ≤ 2}.
M_N(ω) = (sup_{i : Fin N} ENNReal.ofReal(|X_{i.val}(ω)|)).toReal; with finite real-valued coordinates this is the ordinary maximum max_{0≤i<N}|X_i(ω)|.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is an absolute positive real constant C such that, for every probability space and every sequence of measurable real-valued functions whose coordinate exponential-square scales qμ(X_i) have finite uniform supremum K, and for every integer N ≥ 2, the maximum of the absolute values of the first N functions is integrable and has expectation at most C K sqrt(log N). The scale qμ(X_i) is defined exactly as the infimum over nonzero finite extended-nonnegative t for which exp(X_i²/t²) is integrable and has expectation at most 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The assertion applies only under the implication hypotheses: if some X_i is not measurable, K is not strictly below ∞, or N < 2, the corresponding implication is vacuously true.
The measure is required to be a probability measure, not merely finite or σ-finite.
The sequence is indexed by all natural numbers, while M_N uses precisely indices i : Fin N, namely 0 through N-1.
No independence, centering, identical-distribution, or mean-zero assumption is encoded.
The coordinate scale is the literal ENNReal infimum of the specified admissible set. Admissible t must exclude both 0 and ∞, although the infimum itself may equal 0.
Integrability of exp(X_i²/t²) is an explicit part of threshold admissibility, not inferred merely from the numerical integral inequality.
The finite-uniform-scale condition is K < ∞; this makes K.toReal a faithful finite real scale. ENNReal.toReal has a total definition even at ∞, so the hypothesis is semantically important.

LocalDef003 uses ENNReal.toReal after a pointwise supremum. For N ≥ 2 and real-valued coordinates the finite supremum is finite and agrees with the usual maximum, but the raw conversion operation itself is total even at ∞.
The integral operation is total in Lean even for nonintegrable functions, but the theorem separately concludes integrability of M_N.
The factor is exactly sqrt(log of the real cast of N), with no replacement such as sqrt(log(1+N)); N ≥ 2 ensures the usual positive-domain behavior.
The single constant C is chosen before Ω, μ, X, and N, so it is universal and independent of all of them.
